title: Pompeii — the city buried in an afternoon
style: documentary photograph, Roman Italy, hard Mediterranean light, ash grey and terracotta, fine grain, no text, no watermark, no modern objects

lines.vo: On an August morning a Roman town went about its business.
lines.image: a paved street of stone houses under hard morning sun, no people
lines.title: AN ORDINARY DAY

lines.vo: Nobody there had a word for what the mountain was.
lines.image: a broad mountain over a bay, seen from a distance
caption: No word
for volcano.
Not yet.

lines.vo: Just after noon it opened, and threw ash twenty miles up.
lines.image: a towering ash column against a bruised sky

lines.vo: Pumice fell for hours. Roofs took the weight, then gave.
lines.image: a collapsed tiled roof over a stone room, rubble on the floor

lines.vo: What buried them also kept them, exactly where they fell.
lines.image: a plaster cast of a figure lying in a glass case
lines.artefact: a close view of a plaster cast of a curled figure, grey and cracked
caption: Not bones.
The shape
the body left.

lines.vo: Seventeen centuries later somebody dug, and the afternoon was still there.
lines.image: an excavated street trench cut through grey ash
lines.title: SEVENTEEN CENTURIES
